newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunker sales peak in April price trough.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunker sales peak in April price trough.

text.p: The ARA bunker market, centred around Rotterdam, witnessed a surge in liftings in April as suppliers in the area offered the world's cheapest prices.
April loadings in the ARA area totalled around 500,000 tonnes, about 100,000 tonnes higher than in each of the preceding three months, according to most dealers questioned.
The reason for the volume growth is not hard to find. Rotterdam bunker prices have been significantly lower than in all competing ports, reaching 18 month lows towards the end of the month.

"It has been completely triggered by the fact that Rotterdam has been so cheap. We have had quite a number of tankers fixing (bunkers) because of the price difference with Fujairah," said one Rotterdam-based trader.

Fujairah has been at least $8 a tonne higher for the whole month, Singapore has been at least $10 a tonne more expensive, while Houston bunkers proved more competitive, but still ended the month $10 a tonne higher than in Rotterdam.
And the reason for the price differentials has been supply.
"There is so much product including imported cargoes," a bunker trader at one Rotterdam-based major.
Most refineries in the area were running at or near full capacity in April and the substantial regional production was topped up by ample Russian imports.
The lion's share of the business, however, has gone to majors: certain independent players say they are feeling the squeeze.
"Better (volumes)? That wasn't our experience at all," one independent supplier said.
Some independents say the continued desire and capacity of the big players to shift large volumes at prices barely higher than the ex wharf barge prices has left them a very thin slice of the market.
Others say that the prices have been much less volatile in April than in previous months favouring bulk suppliers at the expense of smaller traders.
"There weren't a lot of swings. It's hard to build a strategy around that," one independent trader said.

As in Rotterdam, Antwerp has seen healthy volumes, traders say. In addition, the usual 50 cents/$1 a tonne premium over Rotterdam has been restored. In March oversupply, largely brought about by one trading house, meant Antwerp bunkers traded at a discount to Rotterdam.
